title: Texas Test Prep
subject: Texas History
intro: Spanish Texas, 1754 to 1821: the Seven Years War, the Louisiana Purchase, Father Hidalgo, and the filibusters the Spanish were watching for.

questions.q: The Seven Years War lasted from...
questions.explain: It ran 1754 to 1763.

questions.q: In America the Seven Years War was known as the French and ______ War. (one word)
questions.explain: Americans called it the French and Indian War.

questions.q: After the war, Great Britain gained...
choices: Canada and all land east of the Mississippi
New Orleans and land west of the Mississippi
questions.explain: Britain took Canada plus everything east of the Mississippi River.

questions.q: After the war, Spain got...
choices: New Orleans and French land west of the Mississippi
Canada and land east of the Mississippi
questions.explain: Spain got New Orleans and the French land west of the Mississippi (Louisiana).

questions.q: After the war, France was...
choices: no longer a colonial power in the Americas
the strongest power in the Americas
questions.explain: France lost its land in North America, so it was no longer a colonial power there.

questions.q: Why did losing France as a neighbor change things for Spanish Texas?
choices: Louisiana was now Spain's, so Texas no longer bordered France
questions.explain: With Louisiana in Spanish hands, Texas was no longer a border against France, so Spain rethought how to defend it.

questions.q: Marqués de Rubí said Spain did not have the ______ or ______ to defend all its claims in Texas.
questions.explain: Rubí inspected the frontier and decided Spain lacked the wealth or power to hold it all.

questions.q: Rubí suggested closing all missions EXCEPT those in...
questions.explain: Keep San Antonio and La Bahía, close the rest (the East Texas missions were abandoned and settlers moved to San Antonio).
questions.review: Rubí kept San Antonio + La Bahía

questions.q: Rubí kept the missions in La Bahía and in ______. (two words)
questions.explain: San Antonio, which became the capital of Spanish Texas.

questions.q: In what year did the 13 colonies declare independence from Great Britain?
questions.explain: 1776: the Declaration of Independence.

questions.q: In 1776 the 13 colonies fought for independence from...
questions.explain: They fought Great Britain in the American Revolution.

questions.q: In what year was the Louisiana Purchase? (number)
questions.explain: 1803: the United States bought Louisiana from France (Spain had given it back to France in 1800).

questions.q: The Louisiana Purchase did what to the size of the United States?
questions.explain: It doubled the size of the U.S., for about $15 million.

questions.q: About how much did the U.S. pay for Louisiana?
questions.explain: About $15 million, roughly 3 cents an acre.

questions.q: Why was New Orleans so important to the U.S.?
choices: A free port for trade down the Mississippi
It was the capital of Texas
questions.explain: Farmers shipped goods down the Mississippi to the port of New Orleans; owning it kept trade free.

questions.q: Which expedition explored the Louisiana Purchase?
questions.explain: Lewis and Clark set out in 1804 to explore the new land.

questions.q: Why did the Louisiana Purchase worry Spain about Texas?
choices: The U.S. was now Texas's next-door neighbor
questions.explain: Now Americans bordered Texas, and some, like filibusters, wanted it.

questions.q: Mexicans were becoming unhappy with...
questions.explain: People in New Spain were tired of Spanish rule.

questions.q: Father Miguel Hidalgo y Costilla was a...
questions.explain: Hidalgo was a Catholic priest in the town of Dolores.

questions.q: Hidalgo's 1810 call to fight for independence is called the...
questions.explain: On September 16, 1810 he rang the church bell in Dolores and called people to rise up: the Grito de Dolores.

questions.q: In what year did Hidalgo call for independence? (number)
questions.explain: 1810. Mexico celebrates it every September 16.

questions.q: Which was NOT one of the problems Hidalgo's army had?
questions.explain: His army was mostly farmers and workers: no training, little equipment, little discipline.

questions.q: Name a problem with Hidalgo's army.
questions.explain: No training, no equipment and lack of discipline.

questions.q: What happened to Father Hidalgo in 1811?
questions.explain: After defeats he fled north, was captured and executed in 1811.

questions.q: In what year did Mexico finally win independence?
questions.explain: 1821: ten years after Hidalgo died, and Texas became part of Mexico.

questions.q: Hidalgo is known as the...
questions.explain: Hidalgo's call inspired the whole movement, so he is called the Father of Mexican Independence.

questions.q: Which came FIRST?
Which came LAST?
questions.explain: 1821 is the end of Spanish Texas.

questions.q: In Texas history, a filibuster was someone who...
choices: came from another country and tried to take land and power from the government by force
gave very long speeches to delay a vote
was a Spanish soldier guarding the border
was a priest who started missions
questions.explain: In Spanish Texas a filibuster was a foreign adventurer who came to fight the government for land, power and personal gain. (The long-speech meaning in Congress came later.)

questions.q: Which government decided who counted as a filibuster in Texas? (one word)
questions.explain: Texas belonged to Spain until 1821, so it was the Spanish government that called these intruders filibusters.

questions.q: Criterion 1: a filibuster was from a ______ country (not Spanish).
questions.explain: A filibuster was a foreigner. Someone born in Spain or New Spain could rebel, but would not be called a filibuster.

questions.q: Criterion 2: a filibuster came to ______ the government. (one word)
questions.explain: Filibusters came prepared to fight the Spanish government, usually with a small private army.

questions.q: Criterion 3: a filibuster wanted...
questions.explain: They wanted to grab land and power in Texas for themselves.

questions.q: Criterion 4: a filibuster wanted personal gain, meaning they wanted to...
questions.explain: Personal gain means wealth: filibusters hoped to get rich.

questions.q: How many of the four criteria must a person meet to be a filibuster?
questions.explain: On the worksheet, only people with a check in every column are filibusters. Missing even one (like not fighting the government) makes it a NO.

questions.q: Philip Nolan: filibuster or not?
questions.explain: Nolan was an American horse trader who led armed men into Texas without permission. He meets all four criteria. Spanish troops killed him in 1801.

questions.q: Moses Austin: filibuster or not?
questions.explain: Austin was a foreigner who wanted land and wealth, but he asked Spain for permission to bring settlers (1821). He was not prepared to fight the government, so he is a NO.
questions.review: Moses Austin asked permission, did not fight

questions.q: Peter Ellis Bean: filibuster or not?
questions.explain: Bean was an American who rode with Philip Nolan. He was captured by the Spanish when Nolan was killed. Foreigner, fought, wanted land and gain: all four checks.

questions.q: Barr: filibuster or not?
questions.explain: Barr was a foreigner (an Irish-born trader in Nacogdoches) who wanted land and money, but he traded with Spain's permission instead of fighting it. No fighting, so NO.

questions.q: Father Miguel Hidalgo: filibuster or not?
questions.explain: Hidalgo did fight the government (he started Mexico's war for independence in 1810), but he was born in New Spain, not a foreigner. So he is a NO.
questions.review: Father Hidalgo was not a foreigner

questions.q: James Long: filibuster or not?
questions.explain: Long was an American who led armed expeditions into Texas (starting 1819) and declared Texas independent. All four checks.

questions.q: Jean Lafitte: filibuster or not?
questions.explain: Lafitte was a French-born pirate based on Galveston Island who wanted riches and helped filibusters like James Long. Your worksheet counts him as a filibuster.

questions.q: Father Hidalgo fought the Spanish government. What criterion is he MISSING?
questions.explain: Fighting is not enough. Hidalgo was from New Spain (Mexico), so he fails the 'foreigner' test.

questions.q: Moses Austin and Barr are both NO for the same reason. What is it?
choices: They were not prepared to fight the government
questions.explain: Both were foreigners who wanted land and gain, but they worked with Spain instead of fighting it.

questions.q: Who was Philip Nolan's companion that was captured by the Spanish?
questions.explain: Peter Ellis Bean rode with Nolan in 1801 and spent years as a Spanish prisoner.

questions.q: Which filibuster was a pirate on Galveston Island?
questions.explain: Jean Lafitte ran a pirate base at Galveston.

questions.q: Name one person on the worksheet who is a filibuster.
questions.explain: The four filibusters on the sheet: Philip Nolan, Peter Ellis Bean, James Long and Jean Lafitte.
